source.publication: 2025 Complete Income Tax Instruction Booklet (ip25), Kansas Department of Revenue, with Form K-40 and Schedule S bound in (PDF pages 19-22)
source.section: Form K-40 lines 1-12 (ip25 PDF page 20; exemption block PDF page 19); K-40 instructions lines 1-3 (PDF page 6), line 4 and exemptions (PDF page 6), lines 5-8 (PDF page 7); tax rate schedule: 2025 Tax Computation Worksheet (PDF page 34) and Tax Table (PDF pages 27-34)

worked: Federal AGI = wages (you) 35,765.00 = 35,765.00. Federal taxable income = 35,765.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 (15,750.00) = 20,015.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; federal figures are given, not tested; Kansas starts from federal AGI). No Kansas modifications: Schedule S lines A9 and A26 are 0.00, line A27 net modification 0.00 (the K-40 instructions let a filer skip line 2). Form K-40: line 1 federal AGI 35,765.00; line 2 modifications 0.00; line 3 Kansas AGI = 35,765.00 + (0.00) = 35,765.00; line 4 standard deduction (single) 3,605.00; line 5 exemption allowance (1 exemption) 9,160.00, 0 dependents; line 6 total deductions = 3,605.00 + 9,160.00 = 12,765.00; line 7 taxable income = 35,765.00 - 12,765.00 = 23,000.00; line 8 tax (rate schedule as numbers, PDF page 34): 5.2% x 23,000.00 = 1,196.0000 = 1,196.00. Line 7 is 100,000 or less, so the form reads the tax table: row 22,951-23,000, single, head of household or married filing separate column, PDF page 28, gives 1,195; expected keeps the formula figure. Lines 9-10 do not apply (resident); line 11 0.00; line 12 total income tax 1,196.00. Credits (lines 13-15, 17): none, 0.00; state income tax = 1,196.00. Wages chosen so taxable income is exactly 23,000.00: all at 5.2%, the last dollar of the low band.
accepted_approximations: Tax is computed from the rates, not the printed tables and rounded worksheet subtraction.
